overall: Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating privately after its May 31 hearing outside the public's view and by failing to timely create and approve minutes; no violation found on minute content since the minutes remain drafts.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly met privately to deliberate and approve a development project right after its May 31 hearing, once the public had left the room.
allegations.key_passage: Based on the circumstances, we find that this discussion was not open to the public and therefore find that the Board deliberated outside of an open meeting in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Not alleged in the complaint: whether the Board timely created and approved minutes of its May 31 meeting, with the first draft not received until September 13.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Board violated the law by failing to timely create and approve accurate minutes from this meeting.

allegations.summary: Whether the draft minutes accurately reflected the post-hearing discussion, which the draft omitted.
allegations.key_passage: Because the minutes remain in draft form, we find no violation for the substantive deficiencies

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.

Board members to review Attorney General Open Meeting Law Training Videos #1 (Introduction and Open Meeting Law definitions) and #5 (Meeting Minutes and Records) and certify compliance to the AG's office within thirty days of the letter, using the attached form.
